an6.19:1.1: I have heard that at one time the Blessed One was staying near Nādika in the Brick Hall.
an6.19:1.4: “Yes, lord,” the monks responded to him.
an6.19:1.6: “Mindfulness of death, when developed & pursued, is of great fruit & great benefit. It gains a footing in the deathless, has the deathless as its final end.
an6.19:1.7: Therefore you should develop mindfulness of death.”
an6.19:2.1: When this was said, a certain monk addressed the Blessed One,
an6.19:2.3: “And how do you develop mindfulness of death?”
an6.19:2.5: ‘O, that I might live for a day & night, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal.’
an6.19:2.6: This is how I develop mindfulness of death.”
an6.19:3.1: Then another monk addressed the Blessed One,
an6.19:3.2: “I, too, already develop mindfulness of death.”
an6.19:3.3: “And how do you develop mindfulness of death?”
an6.19:3.5: ‘O, that I might live for a day, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal.’
an6.19:3.6: This is how I develop mindfulness of death.”
an6.19:4.1: Then another monk addressed the Blessed One,
an6.19:4.5: ‘O, that I might live for the interval that it takes to eat a meal, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal.’…”
an6.19:5.1: Then another monk addressed the Blessed One,
an6.19:5.5: ‘O, that I might live for the interval that it takes to swallow, having chewed up four morsels of food, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal.’…”
an6.19:6.1: Then another monk addressed the Blessed One,
an6.19:6.5: ‘O, that I might live for the interval that it takes to swallow, having chewed up one morsel of food, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions.
an6.19:6.6: I would have accomplished a great deal.’…”
an6.19:7.1: Then another monk addressed the Blessed One,
an6.19:7.5: ‘O, that I might live for the interval that it takes to breathe out after breathing in, or to breathe in after breathing out, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal.’
an6.19:7.6: This is how I develop mindfulness of death.”
an6.19:8.1: When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the monks.
an6.19:8.3: ‘O, that I might live for a day & night…
an6.19:10.2: for the interval that it takes to eat a meal…
an6.19:11.2: for the interval that it takes to swallow having chewed up four morsels of food, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal’—
an6.19:12.1: they are said to dwell heedlessly. They develop mindfulness of death slowly for the sake of ending the effluents.
an6.19:13.1: “But whoever develops mindfulness of death, thinking,
an6.19:13.2: ‘O, that I might live for the interval that it takes to swallow having chewed up one morsel of food…
an6.19:14.2: for the interval that it takes to breathe out after breathing in, or to breathe in after breathing out, that I might attend to the Blessed One’s instructions. I would have accomplished a great deal’—
an6.19:15.1: they are said to dwell heedfully. They develop mindfulness of death acutely for the sake of ending the effluents.
an6.19:16.2: ‘We will dwell heedfully. We will develop mindfulness of death acutely for the sake of ending the effluents.’
an6.19:16.3: That is how you should train yourselves.” That is what the Blessed One said. Gratified, the monks delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
